lem-linucb-elliptical-potential:
## Statement

Let $d,n\ge1$, let $\lambda>0$, let $V_0=\lambda I_d$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb R^d$. Define $V_t=V_{t-1}+a_ta_t^{\mathsf T}$ and $u_t=a_t^{\mathsf T}V_{t-1}^{-1}a_t$ for $1\le t\le n$. Then every $V_t$ is positive definite, $u_t\ge0$, and

$$\det V_t=\det V_{t-1}(1+u_t)\quad(1\le t\le n),\qquad \sum_{t=1}^n\min\{1,u_t\}\le2\log\!\left(\frac{\det V_n}{\det V_0}\right).$$
lem-linucb-trace-determinant-bound:
## Statement

Let $d,n\ge1$, let $\lambda>0$, let $L\ge0$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\mathbb R^d$ satisfy $\|a_t\|_2\le L$. Put $V_t=\lambda I_d+\sum_{s=1}^t a_sa_s^{\mathsf T}$ and $V_0=\lambda I_d$, and define $\operatorname{tr}(M)=\sum_{i=1}^d M_{ii}$. Then

$$0<\det V_t\quad(0\le t\le n),\qquad \log\!\left(\frac{\det V_n}{\det V_0}\right)\le d\log\!\left(1+\frac{nL^2}{d\lambda}\right).$$
lem-linucb-predictable-mgf-substitution:
## Statement

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $(\Omega,\mathcal F,P)$ be a probability space, let $\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal F$ be a sub-sigma-algebra, and let $\eta$ be a real random variable such that, for every $q\in\mathbb R$, $e^{q\eta}$ is integrable and

$$\mathbb E[e^{q\eta}\mid\mathcal G]\le e^{q^2/2}\quad\text{almost surely}.$$

Then for every bounded, real, $\mathcal G$-measurable random variable $Q$,

$$\mathbb E[e^{Q\eta-Q^2/2}\mid\mathcal G]\le1\quad\text{almost surely}.$$
def-linear-contextual-bandit-model:
## Definition

Fix integers $d,n\ge1$, real parameters $\lambda>0$, $L\ge1$, and $m_2\ge0$, and a deterministic vector $\theta^*\in\mathbb R^d$ with $\|\theta^*\|_2\le m_2$. Replacing any finite feature bound by its maximum with $1$ makes the convention $L\ge1$ harmless. Work on a probability space with a filtration $(\mathcal F_t)_{t=0}^{n+1}$ satisfying $\mathcal F_t\subseteq\mathcal F_{t+1}$.

At round $t$, before reward noise is observed, the history sigma-algebra $\mathcal F_t$ contains all contexts, choices, and feedback through rounds $s<t$, as well as the current context $C_t$, the nonempty available action set, and its available feature set $\mathcal A_t\subseteq\mathbb R^d$. The features arise from a measurable map $\psi_t$ between spaces with declared measurable structures by $a=\psi_t(C_t,\bar a)$ for available actions $\bar a$. The feature set is finite or compact in the Euclidean topology, every candidate $a\in\mathcal A_t$ satisfies $\|a\|_2\le L$, and the selected feature $A_t=\psi_t(C_t,a_t)\in\mathcal A_t$ is $\mathcal F_t$-measurable. The true-mean maximum is attained and its value is $\mathcal F_t$-measurable. A policy using LinUCB must also select an attained upper-confidence maximizer measurably from the pre-reward information; finite ordered action sets select the first maximizer, while a compact set is used only when such a predictable selection is supplied.

After $A_t$ is selected, the reward $X_t$ is observed, where $\eta_t$ is an $\mathcal F_{t+1}$-measurable real random variable and

$$X_t=\langle\theta^*,A_t\rangle+\eta_t.$$

For every $q\in\mathbb R$, require $e^{q\eta_t}$ to be integrable and its conditional expectation version to satisfy

$$\mathbb E[e^{q\eta_t}\mid\mathcal F_t]\le e^{q^2/2}\quad\text{almost surely}.$$

This is conditional $1$-sub-Gaussian noise with the pre-reward convention for $\mathcal F_t$. No independence between rounds is assumed. For $0\le t\le n$, define the unaveraged ridge information matrix and response sum by

$$V_t:=\lambda I_d+\sum_{s=1}^t A_sA_s^{\mathsf T},\qquad b_t:=\sum_{s=1}^t A_sX_s,$$

with empty sums equal to $0$. Set $\widehat\theta_0=0$ and $\widehat\theta_t=V_t^{-1}b_t$ for $t\ge1$. For a real symmetric matrix $M$ satisfying $v^{\mathsf T}Mv>0$ for all nonzero $v$, write $\|v\|_M:=\sqrt{v^{\mathsf T}Mv}$. The estimate $\widehat\theta_t$ is the unique minimizer of $\sum_{s=1}^t(X_s-\langle\theta,A_s\rangle)^2+\lambda\|\theta\|_2^2$; the sum is not divided by $t$.
lem-linucb-ridge-information-matrix:
## Statement

In the finite-dimensional linear contextual bandit model, for every $0\le t\le n$ the matrix $V_t=\lambda I_d+\sum_{s=1}^tA_sA_s^{\mathsf T}$ is symmetric and satisfies $x^{\mathsf T}V_tx>0$ for every nonzero $x\in\mathbb R^d$. It is invertible, has determinant at least $\lambda^d>0$, and for every $x\in\mathbb R^d$,

$$x^{\mathsf T}V_t^{-1}x\le\frac{\|x\|_2^2}{\lambda}.$$
lem-linucb-ridge-estimates-are-measurabl:
## Statement

In the finite-dimensional linear contextual bandit model, put

$$G_t:=\sum_{s=1}^t A_sA_s^{\mathsf T},\qquad S_t:=\sum_{s=1}^t A_s\eta_s\qquad(0\le t\le n).$$

Give each finite real matrix space its entrywise Euclidean topology and corresponding Borel sigma-algebra. Then $V_t$, $b_t$, $G_t$, $S_t$, and $D_t:=\det(V_t)$ are $\mathcal F_{t+1}$-measurable matrix, vector, or real random elements, and the ridge estimate $\widehat\theta_t=V_t^{-1}b_t$ is an $\mathcal F_{t+1}$-measurable $\mathbb R^d$-valued random element for every $0\le t\le n$.
lem-linucb-gaussian-mixture-supermarting:
## Statement

Assume AC and Countable Choice and the finite-dimensional linear contextual bandit model. Put $S_t=\sum_{s=1}^tA_s\eta_s$, $G_t=\sum_{s=1}^tA_sA_s^{\mathsf T}$, and $V_t=\lambda I_d+G_t$. Let $\mathcal H_t:=\mathcal F_{t+1}$ be the information after round $t$ has been observed. Then

$$Z_t:=\sqrt{\frac{\det(V_0)}{\det(V_t)}}\exp\!\left(\frac12 S_t^{\mathsf T}V_t^{-1}S_t\right),\qquad Z_0:=1,$$

is a nonnegative integrable supermartingale with respect to $(\mathcal H_t)_{t=0}^n$.
alg-linucb:
## Definition

Given the finite-dimensional linear contextual bandit model, a confidence level $\delta\in(0,1)$, and an ordered finite action set or a supplied measurable predictable maximizer for a compact feature set, LinUCB initializes $V_0=\lambda I_d$, $b_0=0$, and $\widehat\theta_0=0$. At each round $t=1,\ldots,n$, it computes

$$\rho_t=\sqrt\lambda\,m_2+\sqrt{2\log(1/\delta)+\log(\det(V_{t-1})/\det(V_0))},\qquad \beta_t=\max\{1,\rho_t^2\},$$

then selects an available feature vector

$$A_t\in\arg\max_{a\in\mathcal A_t}\left\{\langle\widehat\theta_{t-1},a\rangle+\sqrt{\beta_t}\,\|a\|_{V_{t-1}^{-1}}\right\}.$$

After observing reward $X_t$, it updates

$$V_t=V_{t-1}+A_tA_t^{\mathsf T},\qquad b_t=b_{t-1}+A_tX_t,\qquad \widehat\theta_t=V_t^{-1}b_t.$$

Here $V_{t-1}$ is positive definite by the model and the positive ridge parameter. For a finite ordered action set, ties are resolved by taking the first maximizing action; for a compact set, the procedure requires an attained maximizing feature and the stated measurable predictable selector.
thm-self-normalized-linear-confidence-el:
## Statement

Assume AC and Countable Choice and the finite-dimensional linear contextual bandit model. For $\delta\in(0,1)$ and $1\le t\le n$, set

$$\rho_t=\sqrt\lambda\,m_2+\sqrt{2\log(1/\delta)+\log\!\left(\frac{\det V_{t-1}}{\lambda^d}\right)},\qquad C_t=\left\{\theta\in\mathbb R^d:\|\theta-\widehat\theta_{t-1}\|_{V_{t-1}}^2\le\rho_t^2\right\}.$$

Then

$$\mathbb P\{\theta^*\in C_t\text{ for every }1\le t\le n\}\ge1-\delta.$$
thm-linucb-regret:
## Statement

Assume AC and Countable Choice, the finite-dimensional linear contextual bandit model, and LinUCB with $\beta_t=\max\{1,\rho_t^2\}$ as defined in the algorithm. Suppose also that for every round $t$,

$$\sup_{a,b\in\mathcal A_t}\langle\theta^*,a-b\rangle\le1.$$

Define the random pseudo-regret by

$$\widehat R_n:=\sum_{t=1}^n\left(\max_{a\in\mathcal A_t}\langle\theta^*,a\rangle-\langle\theta^*,A_t\rangle\right).$$

Then, with probability at least $1-\delta$,

$$\widehat R_n\le\sqrt{8n\beta_n\log\!\left(\frac{\det V_n}{\det V_0}\right)}\le\sqrt{8dn\beta_n\log\!\left(1+\frac{nL^2}{d\lambda}\right)}.$$
cor-linucb-expected-regret:
## Statement

Assume the hypotheses of the LinUCB high-probability regret theorem, with $d\ge1$, $\lambda>0$, $L\ge1$, $m_2\ge0$, and horizon $n\ge2$. Run LinUCB with $\delta=1/n$. Let $\widehat R_n$ be its random pseudo-regret and define expected pseudo-regret by $R_n:=\mathbb E[\widehat R_n]$. Put

$$q_n:=\log\!\left(1+\frac{nL^2}{d\lambda}\right),\qquad B_n:=\sqrt{8dn\beta_nq_n},$$

where $\beta_n$ is the algorithm's confidence schedule, and set

$$c:=1+\frac{\log(1+L/\lambda)}{\log2},\qquad C_1:=4+2c+\frac{1+2\lambda m_2^2}{\log2},\qquad C:=\sqrt{8C_1c}+\frac{1}{\sqrt2\log2}.$$

Then

$$R_n\le B_n+1\le C\,d\sqrt n\log(nL).$$

This is an expected pseudo-regret bound; it is distinct from a high-probability bound on realized reward regret.
